title: Why does Ramadan move?
It follows the moon, not the sun.
claims_to_verify: A lunar year is about 354 days; a solar year is about 365 days.
So Ramadan shifts about 11 days earlier each year on the Gregorian calendar.
Ramadan cycles through all seasons over roughly 33 years.

scenes.narration: The Islamic calendar follows the moon.
Each month begins when the new moon is sighted.
A lunar year is about three hundred fifty-four days. A solar year is about three hundred sixty-five.
That is roughly eleven days shorter.
So Ramadan arrives about eleven days earlier every year.
And over about thirty-three years, it travels through every season.
